fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Nighttime discrimination of a HAWK display against competing background lighting is a recognized, scheme-relevant safety mechanism whose failure directly threatens stopping decisions on an arterial crossing.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The verbatim quote in EV-US-001 ('Drivers may be confused by competing background visual elements at night' at Speedway Blvd / Rook Ave) directly supports the pivotal driver-confusion claim, satisfying the quote-required threshold.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern under FHWA RSA final-design semantics with no compliance/safety category mixing or invented normative basis.
justifications.recommendation_quality: A reflective border on the signal housing/backplate is a specific, viable, FHWA-recognized conspicuity countermeasure tied to the exact intersection and device.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians are explicitly named as the exposed road users and the scenario links driver detection failure to pedestrian risk during the crossing phase.

justifications.substance: Clearance-interval timing for slow-walking pedestrians at HAWK sites on high pedestrian/bicycle collision locations is a genuine, well-recognized safety issue with a plausible harm mechanism (conflicting release striking stragglers).
justifications.evidence_grounding: EV-US-016 provides a verbatim quote ('The pedestrian clearance interval may be short, particularly for elderly pedestrians') directly supporting the pivotal claim, anchored to the recorded TABLE A.10 system-wide issue for these exact sites.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern asking for verification of design assumptions rather than asserting a MUTCD compliance violation; no conflation of compliance and safety categories.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Reprogramming clearance intervals at all six named sites using a reduced assumed walking speed is specific, actionable, and viable at final-design stage, though citing a numeric walking speed would strengthen it.
justifications.vru_coverage: Vulnerable road users are central to the finding: pedestrians and elderly pedestrians are named road users and the scenario explicitly addresses their exposure during the clearance phase.
